diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..01f915dd5984d40b3f561873a147638323f66a8b 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,9 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are, unless
+    the whole string is in capitals.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +373,67 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        # In an all-caps string, such as the shouted heading 'HELLO WORLD',
+        # capitals don't mark acronyms.
+        return title
+    return _restore_acronyms(title, _separate_words(word))
+
+
+def _separate_words(word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Separate the words in `word` with spaces the same way
+    ``humanize(underscore(word))`` does, but keep the case of the letters.
+    """
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = word.replace("-", "_")
+    word = re.sub(r"_[Ii][Dd]$", "", word)
+    return word.replace("_", " ")
+
+
+def _restore_acronyms(title: str, words: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the all-caps words of `words` back into `title`, which is `words` in
+    title case.
+    """
+    # Combining marks count as part of a word, because changing the case of
+    # some letters adds one (a lowercase dotted capital I is an "i" followed
+    # by a combining dot). That way case changes never move word boundaries.
+    pattern = r"[\w\u0300-\u036f]+"
+    original_words = list(re.finditer(pattern, words))
+    titled_words = list(re.finditer(pattern, title))
+    if len(original_words) != len(titled_words):
+        # Not expected, but never pair up the wrong words.
+        return title
+    result = ''
+    end = 0
+    keep = False
+    for index, (original, titled) in enumerate(
+        zip(original_words, titled_words)
+    ):
+        # A word that directly follows an apostrophe, like the "s" in
+        # "NASA's", belongs to the word before it and only keeps its
+        # capitals if that word does.
+        is_suffix = index > 0 and (
+            words[original_words[index - 1].end():original.start()] == "'"
+        )
+        keep = original.group().isupper() and (keep or not is_suffix)
+        if keep:
+            result += title[end:titled.start()] + original.group()
+            end = titled.end()
+    return result + title[end:]
